faq.question: What file should I send?
faq.answer: A Word document or Google Doc is ideal. Send your final, proofread text, plus any images in the highest quality you have.

faq.question: Which trim size should I choose?
faq.answer: It depends on your genre and page count. 6 × 9 in suits most nonfiction, 5.5 × 8.5 in and 5 × 8 in suit many novels, and 8.5 × 11 in suits workbooks. I can recommend one when you send your manuscript.

faq.question: Can you format for both KDP and IngramSpark?
faq.answer: Yes. Files are prepared to the requirements of the platforms you choose, and I can prepare versions for both.

faq.question: Do I get the ebook and the print book?
faq.answer: If you need both, I prepare a print-ready PDF for paperback or hardcover and a separate ebook file.

faq.question: Can you fix a book that's already published?
faq.answer: Yes. I can reformat an existing interior, fix layout problems or prepare an updated edition.

faq.question: What's the difference between proofreading and copy editing?
faq.answer: Proofreading is the final check for spelling, grammar, punctuation and typos. Copy editing goes deeper and improves sentences for clarity and flow.

faq.question: Will you change my writing style?
faq.answer: No. Proofreading corrects errors only. If a sentence is unclear, I leave a comment instead of rewriting it.

faq.question: How will I see the corrections?
faq.answer: In Word or Google Docs with tracked changes, so you can see, accept or reject every correction.

faq.question: Which English do you use?
faq.answer: American, British or Canadian English. Tell me which one, or I'll follow the style your manuscript already uses.

why.title: A professional finish

why.title: Your voice protected

why.title: Every change visible

who: Your draft is complete but some sentences feel clunky
You want your book to read smoothly before proofreading and formatting
You're publishing nonfiction, self-help or a guide and want it crystal clear
English is not your first language and you want natural-sounding prose
You want consistent style across a long manuscript

faq.question: Is copy editing the same as proofreading?
faq.answer: No. Copy editing improves how sentences read. Proofreading is the final check for small errors. Many books benefit from both.

faq.question: Will you rewrite my book?
faq.answer: No. I edit sentences to make them clearer, but your ideas, structure and voice stay yours.

faq.question: How do I see the edits?
faq.answer: Tracked changes and comments in Word or Google Docs, so you can accept or reject every edit.

faq.question: Should I copy edit before formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. Editing should be finished before formatting, because text changes after layout can move pages around.
